meaning.evidence: All points kept: the compliance burden, Pages' role, FedRAMP, previews and sign-off, and the four static-site advantages ("where you only pay for what you use").

sense.evidence: Most terms fit ("compliance grunt work", "fewer weak spots", "knock up a website"), but "it's easy to get the tick-off on content updates from stakeholders" says "tick-off", which in Australia is a reprimand ("a ticking-off"), not approval.

authenticity.evidence: Natural ("Static websites have a few things going for them", "Steering clear of a traditional CMS means steering clear of headaches"); "knock up a website" may raise a smirk.
